overview: Narrative review with a documented search and purposive selection, organised around four questions: what readiness tools measure, whether scores predict outcomes after transfer, how young people and families experience assessment, and how assessment can be fair for disadvantaged groups.
population: Studies of adolescents aged 12 to 19 with long-term conditions transferring from paediatric to adult care, and of their families and clinicians, published 2010 to 2026 in English.
exposure: Readiness assessment in any form: questionnaires, checklists, structured conversations and adapted or supported tools.
procedures: The lead searches three databases and two grey literature sources with a dated strategy and records it; the transition nurse specialist checks selection for a random 20 percent. Sources are chosen for relevance to the four questions, with priority to measurement studies, prospective prediction studies, qualitative studies of experience and adaptations for disadvantaged groups. Findings are synthesised thematically with the strength of evidence stated for each conclusion.

outcomes.name: Evidence on prediction
outcomes.measure: Direction and strength of association between readiness scores and engagement or disease control after transfer, as reported
outcomes.why: The property on which the clinic's use of scores depends.

outcomes.name: Constructs measured
outcomes.measure: Domains covered by each tool and their measurement properties
outcomes.why: Shows what the score can and cannot mean.

outcomes.name: Experience of assessment
outcomes.measure: Themes from young people's, parents' and clinicians' accounts

outcomes.name: Coverage of disadvantaged groups
outcomes.measure: Number of sources addressing learning disability, low health literacy, language or deprivation

feasibility: Ten weeks of two sessions and nurse specialist support fit a review of about 40 sources.
biasMitigation: Dated search strategy reported in full

summary: Documented narrative review with four questions and explicit handling of contrary evidence.
